blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Aeolian processes refer to wind-driven geomorphic activities including erosion, transportation, and deposition of surface sediments.
Primary favorable conditions include low precipitation, high evaporation rates, lack of surface moisture, and absence of protective vegetation.
Unconsolidated, fine-grained, dry sediment particles (such as sand and silt) are required for effective wind erosion and movement.
Wind transport occurs via three distinct mechanisms: suspension (fine dust), saltation (bouncing sand grains), and surface creep (rolling coarse particles).

blocks.content: Aeolian processes are most effective in arid and semi-arid regions where sparse vegetation cover allows strong winds to erode and transport loose, fine-grained surface sediments.

rows: Removal and wearing down of rock mass by deflation and abrasion
Accumulation and drop of transported sediments when wind velocity decreases
Mushroom Rocks (Gour), Yardangs, Zeugens, Deflation Hollows
Barchans (Crescent dunes), Seif Dunes, Loess Deposits, Transverse Dunes
Coarse abrasive particles scouring base of exposed rocks
Fine to medium sand and silt accumulating around obstacles or flat terrain

items: Saltation is the dominant mode of sediment transport by wind, accounting for nearly 75% to 80% of total sediment movement.
Differentiate between Deflation (lifting and removal of dry, loose dust/sand forming deflation hollows) and Abrasion (sandblasting action by wind-borne sand particles against rock surfaces).
Soil moisture and dense vegetation cover act as the primary natural deterrents against aeolian erosion by binding particles and reducing wind velocity near the surface.
